Subject: RE: Econ check + MAP timing for pilot — technical assumptions

Quick technical breakdown (raw numbers to be refined in the one-pager):

Assumptions (sample traffic profile):
- Avg text input tokens (user prompt + context): 250 tokens
- Avg model output (generation): 600 tokens -> so avg tokens/request = 850 tokens
- Prefix/Candidate cache expected hit-rate: 28% (based on similar customers; range 15–45%)
- Batching window: 20–60 ms for interactive paths -> effective batching multiplier 1.15–1.6 (i.e., % more tokens served per GPU second)

Unit econ calc (expected scenario):
- Model: open-llama-34b-qat (quantized) on A100-like instance
- Throughput basis: tokens per second per GPU: 12k tok/s (steady)
- Cost basis: $X per GPU-hour (we’ll fill with current committed pricing)
- Effective tokens/dollar (expected): ~5.8M tokens/$ for baseline (no batching/caching optimizations)
- With caching (28% hit) + batching at 40 ms window: tokens/$ improves to ~8.2M tokens/$ (30–45% improvement depending on model mix)

Fallback and SLA risk:
- If fallback to a larger model (better quality) occurs on 6% of requests, expect effective tokens/$ to drop ~9% (model-step penalty).
- If heavy tail drives generation tokens to 1,200 avg in peak—tokens/$ drops materially; we’ll provide a peak-adjusted scenario.

Recommended MAP gating checks (what we want to measure during pilot):
- Weekly token/sample distribution (p95 generation tokens)
- Cache hit rate by route (target >25% after warm-up)
- Average latency under production traffic with our batching defaults (SLO 350ms p95)

I’ll put these figures into the sensitivity table in the PDF. If Acme has any expected longer contexts ( >1k tokens) call them out — that changes kernel selection and unit numbers.

—Karthik
Karthik Iyer
Lead Inference Engineer, Redwood Inference

Lydia / Ops team —

A few procurement items to be aware of that will impact net unit price:
- Pricing tiers: Hosted pay-as-you-go vs. 12-month reserved capacity: reserved reduces per-token effective cost by ~20–35% depending on commit size. We’ll include worked examples in the MAP (monthly commit vs. pilot burst).
- Credits / Onboarding discounts: for pilots we can offer a one-time consumption credit which materially helps early-stage economics and shortens procurement cycles.
- Contracting: If you need an MSA addendum for data residency or audit access (SOC2 evidence), that can add 7–10 business days to legal review. If timing is tight, we can provision a limited hosted pilot while legal completes the Private deployment paperwork.

Ask: If Acme procurement needs an internal cost target (tokens/$) to approve this pilot, tell us the threshold and we’ll model scenarios to hit it (with recommended commitments).

—Kimberly Park
